title: Enhanced fluorescent imaging of proteins in live yeast cells using fluorescently labeled scFv
author: Tsirkas, Zur, et al.
materials: Difco™ Yeast Nitrogen Base w/o AAs (YNB)

steps.title: Generate Z‑projection images
steps.instruction: Create maximum‑intensity Z‑projections from each microscopy stack.

steps.title: Export and organize TIFF files
steps.instruction: Export each projection as a single‑channel .tif file, give each a simple distinct name (e.g., image1, image2, …), and move all files into one analysis folder. Do NOT apply any processing (deconvolution, contrast adjustment, etc.) that could alter original pixel intensities.

steps.title: Analyze membrane rings (EldenRing)
steps.instruction: Run the custom MATLAB script “EldenRing” to identify nuclear‑membrane rings and quantify their fluorescence.

substeps.instruction: Activate MATLAB and open the EldenRing script.
Set the image folder path, e.g., Folder = 'C:\path';
Define the image dimension variable W (pixel size of the .tif files).
Crop the image with: img = img(10:(W-10), 10:(W-10));
Detect rings using imfindcircles with minimum/maximum diameters [6 40] and Sensitivity 0.85: [centers,radii] = imfindcircles(img,[6 40],'Sensitivity',0.85);
Run the script in the MATLAB command window; the output is ringsIntensities.xlsx containing file name, average and median nuclear‑membrane intensities, and nucleus diameter for each cell.

steps.title: Analyze fluorescent foci (TokyoGhoulRe)
steps.instruction: Run the custom MATLAB script “TokyoGhoulRe” to locate and quantify fluorescent foci.

substeps.instruction: Install the MIJ package in MATLAB to enable ImageJ/Fiji functions.
Activate MATLAB and open the TokyoGhoulRe script.
Set the image folder path, e.g., Folder = 'C:\path';
Enter the noise threshold X (determined beforehand in ImageJ via Process → Find Maxima) in the command: MIJ.run('Find Maxima', 'noise=X output=List exclude');
Set the pixel number Y and radius Z around each local maximum: pixelNumber = Y; radius = Z;
Define the image dimension variable W and compute usable pixels: (size(img,1) == W); pixels = W - Z;
Run the script in the MATLAB command window; the output is fociIntensities.xlsx containing file names and foci intensities.
NOTE: Use the same noise value X for all images in a given analysis to keep the background‑vs‑signal threshold consistent.

steps.title: Statistical comparison of outputs
steps.instruction: Compare the numeric results (ringsIntensities.xlsx and/or fociIntensities.xlsx) across experimental conditions or strains using appropriate statistical tests (e.g., Student’s t‑test, ANOVA).

steps.title: Plot and present results
steps.instruction: Create the desired graphical representation of the quantified data (histogram, box, swarm, dot, strip, violin plots, etc.) for figures and reporting.
